stories.headline: St Theressa Institute students visit Usman War Memorial along LoC
stories.title: St Theressa Institute students visit Usman War Memorial along LoC
stories.summary: Rajouri, Nov 22: Jhangar Battalion of the Indian Army organised an educational visit for around 200 students of St Theressa Institute of Education, Rajouri, to the Usman War Memorial located along the Line of Control (LoC). The visit aimed at familiarising students with the military history of the region and inspiring them through the courage, leadership and sacrifices of soldiers who defended the nation. During the visit, students were briefed about the “Battle of Nowshera”, fought during the 1947-48 Indo-Pak conflict. They were informed about the challenging circumstances faced by the Indian Army and the determined resistance offered by troops to defend Nowshera and adjoining areas. Special emphasis was laid on the role of Brigadier Mohammad Usman, popularly known as the 'Lion of Nowshera'. Students were apprised of his exemplary leadership, courage and ultimate sacrifice in the line of duty while defending the strategic Nowshera sector. They were also briefed about the historical significance of the Usman War Memorial and the importance of preserving the legacy of soldiers who laid down their lives in the service of the nation. The interaction highlighted values of discipline, courage, perseverance, leadership and selfless service, while encouraging students to learn from history and become responsible citizens. Organised under the theme 'Know Your History, Be Inspired for Tomorrow', the initiative provided students an opportunity to experience history beyond textbooks and develop a deeper understanding of the sacrifices made by the Armed Forces. “The visit was part of Jhangar Battalion's continued efforts to connect with the local community, promote awareness about the region's military heritage and inspire younger generations through stories of valour and sacrifice,” the Army spokesperson said.

stories.headline: 'India-Russia ties an 'added value', can help end war'
stories.title: 'India-Russia ties an 'added value', can help end war'
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: New Delhi: The Netherlands sees India's continued engagement with Russia as an "added value," as it believes New Delhi can use its ties with Moscow to persuade it to end the Ukraine war, Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen said on Sunday.
Berendsen is on an official visit to India from November 22 to 23.
He co-chaired the inaugural Foreign Ministers' Meeting with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar in New Delhi on Sunday and reviewed the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership.

"We understand that India has its own history, its own role in the world and its own relations," Berendsen told PTI, responding to a question on India's strategic autonomy and its continued engagement with Moscow.

"We actually see it as an added value of our relationship with India that it has a relationship with Russia and can also use that relation to show Russia that it needs to put an end to this war and accept a ceasefire," he said.
The Russia-Ukraine war, in its fifth year, continues with intensified attacks from both sides.
Russia has stepped up strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, while US-brokered peace talks have made little progress beyond a prisoner swap.

Berendsen said India and the Netherlands, as trading countries, shared concerns over maritime security and freedom of navigation, and needed to work together to address challenges in an increasingly uncertain world.
"I think we're dealing with the same challenges: how to decrease dependencies, how to be more strategically autonomous on critical raw materials, technology and energy," he said.
"If you want to do that, you need to diversify, which means new partnerships.
I think the Netherlands, the EU and India are doing exactly that," he added.
On trade, he described the proposed India-European Union free trade agreement, expected to be signed in December, as a crucial step that could open opportunities beyond merchandise trade.

stories.headline: BJD accuses Odisha govt of using foreign visit probe to divert attention from flood crisis
stories.title: BJD accuses Odisha govt of using foreign visit probe to divert attention from flood crisis
stories.summary: BJD leaders accused the Odisha government of using an inquiry into Naveen Patnaik's foreign visits to divert attention from flood management failures and other governance issues.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: BJD leaders accused the Odisha government of using an inquiry into Naveen Patnaik's foreign visits to divert attention from flood management failures and other governance issues.

Bhubaneswar: The Opposition Biju Janata Dal (BJD) has targeted the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Odisha government, alleging that the inquiry into alleged irregularities in the foreign visits of former Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik and others during the previous state government was ordered to divert public attention from the principal opposition party's criticism of the current state government over the recent devastating floods across the state.

Addressing a press conference in Bhubaneswar on Sunday, BJD MLA and party's general secretary Goutam Buddha Das and spokesperson Lenin Mohanty said the party welcomed the inquiry into the foreign visits of former Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik and his close aide and the then Private Secretary to Patnaik, V.K. Pandian.
Das alleged that the Odisha government is using the issue to divert attention from the double-engine government's failures in disaster management, law and order and pension distribution.
He said the state government has rejected a proposal by the BJD for a discussion in the Odisha Assembly on the devastating floods in Ganjam district, fearing that its shortcomings would be exposed.
"The Government is nervous that people will come to know the truth.
The Double-Engine Government has failed in several areas, including law and order, distribution of social security pensions and flood management.
To divert public attention from its failures, the state government has brought up an irrelevant issue in the form of an inquiry," Das added.
The senior BJD leader alleged that previous inquiries ordered into three issues targeting the regional party and its leaders have also failed to establish any wrongdoing.
Referring to the Jagannath Temple's Ratna Bhandar controversy, Das said that BJP leaders had alleged before the elections that its valuables were looted and taken to Tamil Nadu.
However, the state government later confirmed that all valuables are safe.
The BJD leader also cited the allegations over Pandian's helicopter visits, saying the inquiry and subsequent court proceedings has given him a clean chit.

stories.headline: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.title: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.summary: The talks focused on establishing engagement protocols, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, and maintaining open communication channels
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India and China have concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and putting in place measures to prevent friction between troops deployed along the frontier ahead of the onset of harsh winter conditions.
Sources in the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the closely guarded discussions, which began on November 8, 2026, a day after Deepavali, continued for nearly 10 days, with a short break in between.
The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully.
Lieutenant-General Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Army’s III Corps, also known as the Spear Corps, led the Indian delegation.
The formation is headquartered at Rangapahar near Dimapur in Nagaland.
His Chinese counterpart and other military officers participated in the discussions.
An official from the Ministry of External Affairs was also present.

The latest round of talks primarily focused on establishing engagement protocols between the two sides, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, maintaining open communication channels and reducing tensions in the eastern sector.
Both countries have deployed substantial numbers of troops in the region.

The discussions assume significance as winter conditions along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh can become extremely severe, posing considerable challenges to troop sustenance, movement and logistical support.
Any delay in implementing the measures discussed could complicate the situation on the ground as temperatures fall and access to forward areas becomes increasingly difficult.
The second round follows the first Corps Commander-level meeting, held on September 6 and 7, 2026, at the Wacha-Damai Border Personnel Meeting (BPM) point in the Kibithoo sector.

stories.headline: Punjab’s crises call for a plan. Election is an opportunity
stories.title: Punjab’s crises call for a plan. Election is an opportunity
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The election scene is otherwise worrying.
Animosities between parties and individual leaders have vitiated the political environment.
Vicious personal allegations have crowded out informed debate about progressive policies.

Larger issues — such as the failure to diversify the agricultural economy, drug addiction, industrial stagnation, joblessness, environmental degradation, carcinogenic subsoil water, falling standards of health and education, rampant corruption, political violence, gangsterism, and the abuse of state power — frame the story of a state in decline.
Those aspiring to lead Punjab must unfold an honest and doable plan of action for the state’s long-delayed renewal.
This must go beyond unsustainable promises of freebies at the cost of perpetual indebtedness and making people permanently dependent on the largesse of a bankrupt state.
But this is possible only when the rehbars (leaders) rise above rancid partisanship and the pursuit of power for its own sake.
The election is an opportunity for parties to reestablish their credentials as honest proponents of their professed ideologies and public service by focusing on the people’s core issues.

As Alexis de Tocqueville, the French philosopher and statesman, wrote, it is the people who “hover above the entire life of the State… as the cause and end of all things, as the point from which everything emanates and to which everything returns…”.
It is also incumbent on parties to put up candidates who are known for their generosity of heart and largeness of vision and have a view of politics founded in public service.

The oft-repeated statement that only winning candidates will be given party tickets must mean that only those committed to selfless service and humility in their interactions with the people will be selected.
This carries a corresponding obligation on the voters’ part to elect candidates with impeccable credentials of service and integrity.

stories.headline: J&K’s 3014-MW Chenab power push faces delays
stories.title: J&K’s 3014-MW Chenab power push faces delays
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 22: Jammu and Kashmir's ambitious hydropower expansion in the Chenab basin is progressing unevenly, with two major projects approaching completion while the remaining two have recorded less than 42 percent physical progress, according to the latest government monitoring report. The four projects, with a combined installed capacity of 3014 MW, have witnessed a cumulative cost escalation of Rs 5737.29 crore over their original estimates, while the commissioning timelines of the projects reflect significant delays. The September 2026 Flash Report of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) shows that the 1000 MW Pakal Dul Hydroelectric Project has achieved 89 percent physical progress, while the 624 MW Kiru project has reached 92.10 percent. In contrast, the 850 MW Ratle Hydroelectric Project has recorded only 33.14 percent progress, while the 540 MW Kwar project has achieved 41.55 percent. The report, updated with information received up to October 23, puts cumulative expenditure on the four projects at Rs 18,078.10 crore against their combined revised estimated cost of Rs 27,945.06 crore. The projects were originally estimated to cost Rs 22,207.77 crore, indicating an increase of around 25.8 percent. The 1000 MW Pakal Dul project, being executed by NHPC through Chenab Valley Power Projects Limited (CVPPL), has recorded expenditure of Rs 10,038.05 crore against its revised cost of Rs 12,728 crore. Its original estimated cost of Rs 8112.12 crore has increased by Rs 4615.88 crore. Kiru, with an installed capacity of 624 MW, has achieved 92.10 percent physical progress, with cumulative expenditure of Rs 4196.07 crore against its revised estimated cost of Rs 5409 crore. Its original cost of Rs 4287.59 crore has increased by Rs 1121.41 crore. While the MoSPI report lists December 2026 as the revised completion target for both projects, NHPC's November 5 investor conference call outlined a more detailed commissioning schedule. According to the company, Pakal Dul is expected to be fully commissioned by June 2027, with two units targeted for commissioning by March 2027. Reservoir filling is planned to begin towards the end of December 2026. For Kiru, reservoir filling was scheduled to begin in November 2026, with all units targeted for commissioning by March 2027. An official involved with the projects was quoted in a November 11 media report as saying that the “process of commissioning both the 624 MW Kiru and 1,000 MW Pakal Dul project has started”. The progress of Ratle and Kwar remains considerably behind the other two projects. The 850 MW Ratle project, originally scheduled for completion in February 2026, has had its revised deadline extended to November 2028. It has recorded cumulative expenditure of Rs 1743.87 crore against its estimated cost of Rs 5281.94 crore, with physical progress standing at 33.14 percent. NHPC informed investors that dam concreting at Ratle commenced on November 2 and that the project remains targeted for completion by November 2028. Similarly, the 540 MW Kwar project has achieved 41.55 percent physical progress, with expenditure of Rs 2100.11 crore against its estimated cost of Rs 4526.12 crore. Its completion deadline, originally November 2026, has been revised to March 2028 in the MoSPI report. However, NHPC's November 5 conference call indicated a commissioning schedule of May 2028. Unlike Pakal Dul and Kiru, the estimated costs of Ratle and Kwar have remained unchanged, with no cost escalation reflected in the latest report. The Ministry of Power, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha on July 20, 2026, attributed the delays to several project-specific challenges. For Pakal Dul, these included an initial delay due to a court case during the tendering process, the COVID-19 pandemic, a major slope failure at the adit tunnel site of the tunnel boring machine, labour union strikes, frequent tool stoppages, delays in providing encumbrance-free land and agitations by residents and project-affected families. Kiru faced road damage due to floods, road blockages, labour strikes and delays in the supply of dam tower crane components from different countries during the pandemic. For Ratle, the government cited high monsoon discharge, breached dykes, flooding of diversion tunnels, restrictions on blasting near inhabited areas and land-related disturbances involving residents. Kwar, meanwhile, faced delays in awarding hydro-mechanical and electro-mechanical work packages, besides labour strikes and frequent work stoppages. The four projects are expected to add 3014 MW to Jammu and Kashmir's installed hydropower capacity once completed. Their progress remains crucial to the region's efforts to expand electricity generation and reduce dependence on power purchases.

stories.headline: The Book and the Belonging
stories.title: The Book and the Belonging
stories.summary: At the November 16, 2026 launch of Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Mrs Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’ in a five-star hotel in New Delhi, the presence of I.N.D.I.A bloc leaders alongside Congress figures and an odd newly baptised BJP leaders, projected multiple political and personal messages. Different political observers, parties, and commentators interpreted the event differently. However, despite Mrs Gandhi stressing the book - as the word ‘Belonging…’ reflected- is a personal account more focused on Nehru-Gandhi family, it could not escape creating a strong political imprint. The imprint was based on the opposition unity jigsaw which saw a fine-print unfolding in the shape of who-is-who of I.N.D.I.A bloc partners in attendance to give political strength to the function which the author and the organisers must have cherished. In fact, the political flavour dominated the social colouring which might or might not be to the liking of Mrs Gandhi. Samajwadi Party chief and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Mr Akhilesh Yadav sounded sanguine and amply conveyed the spirit and environment of the book release function in his thoughts, he penned down at the book launch. “Let us come together and write a book in which we write a revolution of change.” It was a political message obliquely hinting at the electoral battles, particularly coming Uttar Pradesh assembly polls, ahead. No doubt, he also wrote on the virtues of books and publishing but this observation conveyed the basic spirit and purpose behind lining up the I.N.D.I.A combine leadership. Ostensibly, a painstaking effort had gone into organising the function to its finer details right from the guest list to the sitting arrangement with entire focus on opposition unity. The plan seemed less on arrogance, as the allies have often accused the Congress of, and more on displaying a spirit of accommodation and dignity towards allies, mostly regional parties and much smaller in size, than the Grand Old Party (GOP) dominating the scene, as had been the practice in the past. In fact, it was in continuation of the Congress-planned framework seen during the last few programmes aimed at reflecting I.N.D.I.A groupings unity. This continuity is seen in the Opposition camps attempts at delivering message of bonding at short intervals so as not to give rivals any chance at talking about disunity and differences in the grouping’s ranks delaying their meeting. This bonding was reflected during the last two shows - the rally at the Ramlila Maidan over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the march to Supreme Court of India to file a joint petition, by the I.N.D.I.A partners in this regard. stories.headline: Gold price dip brings buyers back to Kashmir markets
stories.title: Gold price dip brings buyers back to Kashmir markets
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 22: A sharp correction in gold prices has brought buyers back to Kashmir's jewellery markets, with dealers reporting improved demand after months of subdued purchasing activity amid continuously rising rates. The decline has provided relief to families preparing for weddings, for whom gold jewellery remains an important part of marriage-related expenditure. Besides its traditional significance, gold is also widely regarded as a store of wealth and a hedge against inflation and economic uncertainty. However, the sustained rise in prices had increasingly become a source of concern for households, particularly middle-class families struggling to manage wedding expenses. Many had postponed purchases or reduced the quantity of jewellery they intended to buy. Bashir Ahmad, a gold dealer in Srinagar, said customer enquiries and purchases had increased after the recent price correction. He said demand had remained subdued when gold was becoming increasingly expensive, as many customers preferred to wait for a more favourable rate. According to him, the recent decline has encouraged buyers who had postponed their purchases to return to jewellery shops, particularly those with wedding-related requirements. The change in market sentiment is also reflected in individual buying decisions. Shaista was among the customers who purchased gold following the recent fall in prices, while Aijaz Ahmad purchased a one-gram PAMP gold bar for investment purposes. Aijaz's purchase also reflects how gold buying in Kashmir extends beyond jewellery and wedding requirements, with some consumers preferring small quantities of physical gold as a means of preserving savings. The latest correction has brought 24-carat gold prices in Srinagar down to around Rs 1,25,100 per 10 grams, while 22-carat gold, commonly used for jewellery, was quoted at approximately Rs 1,14,690 per 10 grams, according to indicative market rates. The decline is significant compared to November 12, when 24-carat gold was quoted at Rs 1,39,820 per 10 grams and 22-carat gold at Rs 1,28,240. Over the 10 days, 24-carat gold has declined by Rs 14,720, while 22-carat gold has become cheaper by Rs 13,550, representing a fall of more than 10 percent in both categories. The correction follows a sharp sell-off in international bullion markets. Gold futures on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) settled at Rs 1,21,949 per 10 grams on November 20, down Rs 5503, or 4.32 percent, from the previous close. Market analysts have attributed the decline to a stronger US dollar, rising bond yields and expectations of a tighter monetary policy by the US Federal Reserve. Higher interest rates generally reduce gold's attractiveness relative to interest-bearing investments. For Kashmir's households, however, gold occupies a different place in financial and social life. While wedding purchases remain an important driver of demand, families have traditionally considered the precious metal a form of household savings that can be relied upon during financial uncertainty. The recent correction has therefore brought some breathing space for buyers who were finding it increasingly difficult to purchase gold at elevated prices. Dealers say the improvement in demand is encouraging, although the sustainability of the recovery will depend on how international bullion prices move in the coming weeks. With gold prices remaining volatile, consumers are continuing to watch the market closely before committing to larger purchases. The latest decline has nevertheless revived buying interest in a market where soaring prices had increasingly kept prospective customers away. The actual amount paid by consumers varies according to purity, making charges, wastage and applicable taxes.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu seeks stay on Supreme Court order in deepathoon row, says it would ‘alter position irreversibly’
stories.title: Tamil Nadu seeks stay on Supreme Court order in deepathoon row, says it would ‘alter position irreversibly’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Tamil Nadu Commissioner for Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowment Department has moved the Supreme Court seeking a stay of its interim direction of last week permitting the lighting of the ceremonial lamp, identified by worshippers as “deepathoon” (lamp pillar) in Madurai on November 24, contending that it would lead to irreversible consequences.

In a petition seeking part review of the November 20 order, pertaining to the ritual linked to the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple on the Thiruparankundram hills, the Commissioner submitted that “this Hon’ble Court has itself observed that the performance of the ceremony, once permitted, cannot be undone”.

“If the ceremony is performed on 24.11.2026, the subject matter of the present Review Petition will cease to exist, and no order which this Hon’ble Court may thereafter pass, however favourable to the Review Petitioner, will be capable of restoring the position.
The injury is therefore irreparable in the strictest sense of that term,” the review petition said.
The Commissioner contended: “…the balance of convenience lies wholly in favour of the Review Petitioner.
No devotee is denied the festival, and no observance is interrupted.
If interim relief is refused, a long-standing position is altered irreversibly, at a site in close proximity to the Dargah, upon a claim which is yet to be established upon evidence before any forum.
The lamp has never, to this date, been lit at the summit of the Hill.”
The petition said: “The direction therefore preserves nothing; it creates something new.
If it is not lit at the stone pillar this year, the writ petitioners lose nothing they have ever had, and the festival proceeds at the customary location exactly as in every preceding year.”

It contended that the November 20 order suffers from an error as it provides the relief despite saying that it does not amount to a finding that the stone pillar in question is indeed the “deepathoon”, and that the permission is not in recognition or enforcement of any asserted right.

“A strong prima facie case for review has been made out…Paragraph 15 (of the November 20 order) expressly declines to find that the stone pillar is, or has historically been, a place of customary religious observance, and Paragraph 13 records that the permission is not in recognition or enforcement of any asserted right.

stories.headline: High Court upholds 2.5 lakh penalty over energising fuel station without NoC
stories.title: High Court upholds 2.5 lakh penalty over energising fuel station without NoC
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 22: The High Court of J&K and Ladakh has upheld Rs 2.5 lakh penalty imposed on Indian Oil Corporation for energising a petrol pump in Pulwama district’s Lethpora without final access permission from the National Highway Administration. A bench of Justice Sanjay Dhar, while deciding a plea, however, directed the District Magistrate Pulwama, to conduct an inquiry into whether the petrol pump operated under the name of M/s Fatima Filling Station and if the same had been established at the sanctioned location after obtaining all requisite No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from the concerned departments. The Court also directed the district administration to remove encroachments, if any, on the land of the National Highway that are obstructing the construction of an access road to the petrol pump strictly in accordance with law. In a plea, the aggrieved petitioner had called in question a communication dated July 28, 2025, whereby the National Highway Authority (NHA) directed the Chief Manager, Retail Sales, Indian Oil Corporation, to deposit a penalty of Rs 2.5 lakh for energising the fuel station without obtaining the final NOC. The NHA also directed the Corporation to de-energise the retail outlet until the grant of final access permission. The petitioner’s argument was that the petrol pump was set up after obtaining necessary clearances under the Petroleum Act, 1934, and Petroleum Rules, 2002, besides securing provisional access permission from the NHA in 2021. Furthermore, the petitioner contended that the final access permission could not be obtained because of encroachments by local residents and shopkeepers on National Highway land, which, she claimed, the authorities had failed to remove despite repeated requests. In its response, the NHA, however, maintained that the petrol pump had been energised and commercial operations commenced without obtaining final access permission, in violation of the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways on June 26, 2020. Underscoring that the guidelines clearly prohibit energising a fuel station on the basis of provisional access permission and permit such operations only after grant of regular access permission, the court upheld the penalty. It noted that without constructing the access to the petrol pump, the same could not be energized in any circumstances whatsoever. The Court, however, recorded that the petitioner had been unable to construct the access road as neither the NHA nor the district administration had succeeded in removing the encroachments. These circumstances, it said, could provide justification for seeking an extension of provisional access permission and additional time for construction of the approach road, but could not justify operating the petrol pump without final permission. The Court observed that the encroachments were required to be removed in accordance with the provisions of the Control of National Highways (Land and Traffic) Act, 2002. The District Magistrate was vested with powers under Sections 26, 27, 36 and 43 of the Act to facilitate swift removal of encroachments on National Highway land, the court said. The Court held that the District Magistrate, Pulwama in keeping with the Supreme Court's directions in Gyan Prakash vs Union of India, was duty-bound to ensure removal of all encroachments obstructing construction of the access to the petrol pump. The bench directed the District Magistrate to hold an inquiry and if it was established that the petitioner had fulfilled all statutory requirements and obtained the requisite NOCs, she should be allowed to operate the petrol pump at the sanctioned location. Thereafter, upon construction of the access road, the NHA shall grant the necessary final access permission and allow energisation of the outlet, it said. The Court, however, ordered that if any deficiencies were found, the petitioner should be given an opportunity to rectify those, failing which the petrol pump be closed down or sealed.

stories.headline: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
stories.title: FSSAI sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 22: Food regulator FSSAI on Sunday said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after finding its sample of packaged drinking water "unsafe". In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water". A regulatory sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" was collected from the premises of Bisleri International for analysis. "The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," the regulator said. Upon appeal by the company, the sample was sent to the referral food laboratory, which also declared it "unsafe" due to the detection of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator added. The findings of the lab established violations relating to unsafe food under the law. Hence, the FSSAI said it has granted sanction to launch prosecution under the FSS Act, 2006, against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd. During this calendar year, the FSSAI has stepped up enforcement actions against food business operators as well as e-commerce companies. The regulator has also cracked down on energy drink and alcoholic beverage makers.

stories.headline: Nepal Prime Minister to hold delegation-level talks with PM Modi today
stories.title: Nepal Prime Minister to hold delegation-level talks with PM Modi today
stories.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi to discuss bilateral ties, trade, energy, connectivity, flood reconstruction and regional cooperation.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi to discuss bilateral ties, trade, energy, connectivity, flood reconstruction and regional cooperation.

New Delhi: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday, during which the two leaders will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest, according to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).

"During the visit, Shah will hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Modi on November 23 and discuss a range of issues of mutual interest," Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said earlier at a press briefing.
Following the bilateral talks, the two leaders will jointly address a press conference.
Prime Minister Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of the Nepali Prime Minister and his delegation on the same day.
Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day State visit to India at the invitation of Prime Minister Modi.
Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada welcomed him at the airport.
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar is also scheduled to pay a courtesy call on Prime Minister Shah during his visit.
Shah will additionally call on President Droupadi Murmu.

The Nepali Prime Minister is accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Chief Advisor to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior government officials, forming a 35-member government delegation.
A separate 52-member delegation comprising business representatives will also participate in the visit at their own expense.

According to Nepali officials, securing additional air entry routes from India, obtaining substantial financial assistance for reconstruction following the devastating floods of August 26, and securing concessions from India on trade and transit are among the key priorities of the Nepali government.
